Agnostic

/ag-NOS-tik/ - the stress falls on NOS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Agnostic means believing that the existence of God cannot be proven or disproven.

Somewhere in his fifties the barber went agnostic: ask about God while he trims and he claims neither a yes nor a no, because the proof he would need, he says, is not the kind this world supplies.

Worked Example

Past midnight, my roommates went back and forth over theology and cold tea - one quoting proofs of design, the other proofs of absence. Sam, the physics major, refused both chairs. He was agnostic, he said: for him to say yes, or to say no, something would have to count as a test of God - and nothing ever could. So he claimed nothing, and poured more tea.

Agnostic is precise here because Sam isn't wavering and isn't disbelieving - he holds the question itself to be beyond evidence. An atheist claims an answer (no); a believer claims an answer (yes); the agnostic claims the question can't be answered. That's a position, not a shrug.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

noncommittal: Noncommittal means refusing to state a position - a shrug in word form - whatever you may privately believe. Agnostic is not a dodge: it openly stakes a claim, that this question cannot be settled by evidence at all. The noncommittal speaker hides a view; the agnostic announces one.

neutral: Neutral means taking no side in a dispute, often to stay fair or above the fray - a referee is neutral by role. Agnostic is not about sides at all: it is a considered claim that the question itself can never be settled by any evidence.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

certain: convinced the question has an answer they know

devout: firmly and actively committed to belief

Where it sits · how far any answer is ruled out — open-minded → undecided → agnostic

open-minded vs. agnostic: An open-minded juror can still be won over by either side; agnostic goes further, holding that on this question no ruling can ever be reached.

undecided vs. agnostic: An undecided voter expects to choose by Election Day; the agnostic position is stronger - it says the deciding evidence can never arrive at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: not, without

Root — gnost

Root — gnost: knowing

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: A- (not, without) + gnost (knowing) + -ic (relating to) = relating to not-knowing. Greek gnosis meant 'knowledge'; the biologist Thomas Huxley coined agnostic in 1869 for his position that the existence of God lies beyond human knowing - not denied, not affirmed, but unknowable.

Use the root in a new word: diagnosis

Use the root in a new word: diagnosis: The rash and the fever led the pediatrician to a quick diagnosis.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / precise

Agnostic makes a strong, specific claim: not 'I haven't decided' but 'this question cannot be settled by evidence.' Say undecided for a mind still choosing, and dubious - another word in this unit - when the doubt leans toward disbelief. Everyday tech talk uses agnostic loosely ('platform-agnostic'), but in careful writing keep it for questions held to be unanswerable.
